panel_kit.material: kit_panel (2048^2 atlas: albedo, normal, ORM) + kit_city (second 2048^2 atlas, used by the brick_*, wall_shopfront*, sign_*, roof_*, collapse_* pieces; see tools/blender/env/city_kit_atlas.py) + kit_damage (third 2048^2 atlas: facade cells of the *_holed_v2/_v3, *_destroyed_v2/_v3 variants; tools/blender/env/kit_damage_atlas.py)

damage_variants.pattern: <type>_<holed|destroyed>_<v2|v3>; the plain <type>_holed / <type>_destroyed pieces are variant v1
damage_variants.normalisation: same frame as <type>_intact: the game must use the *_intact offset for the variants too (buildKit regex /_(intact|damaged|holed|destroyed)(_v\d+)?$/ when computing the base name)
damage_variants.holed_v2: off-centre shell hole + corner bite + spalled face (panel: outer concrete leaf gone, mineral wool exposed with the outer mesh across it; brick: outer half-brick wythe gone); rebar bent inwards (hit from outside)
damage_variants.holed_v3: hole through the spandrel / half-panel blow-out / big off-centre hole; panels also get a through-crack (split piece displaced ~2 cm outwards where it separates); rebar bent outwards (interior blast)
damage_variants.destroyed_v2: blown-out panel: wide ragged remnant column on one side, thin ragged lintel band snapped through in places, low kerb; panel fragment hanging on its bars below the band; balcony root stub on balcony types
damage_variants.destroyed_v3: blown-out panel: wide lintel band, spandrel remnant rising towards a column on the other side; panel fragment swung out on its bars from the column edge
damage_variants.structure: every *_destroyed piece (v1 too) is framed by the ceiling-slab edge (y H-0.228..H+0.004, ragged front ~5-11 cm behind the facade, torn bars hanging) and a floor screed edge at y 0..0.02 (z -0.05..-1.2); large-panel pieces also show the transverse wall ends (x 0..0.08 and W-0.08..W, z -0.3..-1.25, wallpapered room faces). The slab band covers the interior slab box of buildings.js buildInterior() at the facade.

panel_kit.coords: glTF Y-up. Wall pieces: x 0..W, y 0..H, z 0 (outside face, +Z normal) .. -T (room side). Accessories (balcony*, entrance_canopy) start at the wall face z=0 and extend to +Z.

notes.wall_*_intact: exactly fills [0,W]x[0,H]x[-T,0] -> game normalisation offset is zero
notes.damage_states: all four states share the intact frame; damaged/holed/destroyed may protrude to +Z (curtains, rebar, door leaves, balcony stub) and -Z (room-side debris, radiators) by design
notes.wall_balcony_holed: includes the broken-off root of the balcony slab (game removes balcony_slab at state>=2)
notes.balcony_slab: mixed corrugated asbestos parapet + residents' glazing (wood/PVC/boarded). Variants balcony_slab_open, balcony_slab_glazed are extra (same placement rules) for the game to randomise
notes.balcony_hanging: hinge (wall face, slab top) is at local y = bbox_max.y - 0.14 relative to bbox min; game normalises minY=0 so place it at floor_y - (bbox height - 0.14) to keep the hinge at the slab line
notes.entrance_canopy: slab bottom at bbox minY+0.06 (lamp housing hangs 6 cm below the slab)
notes.roof_parapet: height 0.72 m + galvanised cap; roofing upturn on the room side (-Z)
notes.slab_floor: 3.2 x 0.22 x 3.2 m (x, y, -z). Top = linoleum, bottom = whitewashed ceiling. slab_floor_broken: outer half hinged down 35 deg on its bottom rebar
notes.stair_core: 3.2 wide x 2.8 high x 4.5 deep: flight up from z=-4.2 (floor landing provided by slab_floor) to the half-landing at y=1.4 against the facade, second flight back up to y=2.8
notes.plinth: 3.2 x 0.9 x 0.45 basement plinth with vent grille, same pivot rules as walls
notes.partition_wall_*: interior gypsum partition 3.2 x 2.58 x 0.08 with doorway; _intact/_holed
notes.debris_*: loose furniture debris (wardrobe, bed, table+chair, radiator), origin on the floor
notes.brick_<type>_<state>, brick_red_<type>_<: series 1-447 brick walls, types window/balcony/blank_end/entrance, same 3.2 x 2.8 x 0.3 frame, openings and 4 damage states as wall_*; brick_* = white silicate brick, brick_red_* = red ceramic brick (two piece sets, same geometry, different atlas cells). Reuse balcony_slab*/entrance_canopy/plinth. Holes are stair-stepped along the brick courses; masonry mesh wires instead of rebar
notes.brick_parapet, brick_red_parapet: brick roof parapet 0.69 m with corbelled course + galvanised cap; wall frame (maxZ = 0)
notes.wall_shopfront_<state>, wall_shopfront_s: ground-floor shop panel (converted flat): tiled piers + glazed door + 2x2 display window / one wide opening with a steel roller shutter (closed when intact, half-raised and torn when damaged, ripped out when holed). Fascia y 2.08..2.8 is left for a sign_* piece. Same frame and states as wall_*
notes.sign_<shop>_intact|_damaged: shop sign mounted on the fascia: place in panel coords with its bottom at y = 2.14 on a wall_shopfront* panel. Authored in the accessory frame (centred on x = W/2, starts at the wall face z = 0, extends +Z up to 0.17) -> normalise like balcony/entrance_canopy (add ^sign_ to the accessory regex in buildKit). Shops: apteka, produkty, khlib, magazyn, perukarnia, gospodarchi, kafe, kvity, ovochi, zootovary. _damaged = right bracket torn, hanging tilted (shares the _intact offset)
notes.roof_machine_room, roof_vent, roof_anten: roof-top pieces, origin at their footprint centre on the roof surface (y = 0), +Z front (machine-room door). Place on the roof slab of 9+ storey blocks (machine room above a stair core). buildKit normalises them to minX=0/minY=0/maxZ=0: add bbox_min.x / bbox_max.z back to recentre
notes.collapse_pile_large, collapse_pile_small: section-collapse rubble: pancaked floor slabs on a rubble mound with rebar, standing facade remnants, leaning/lying panels, balcony, furniture. Origin = footprint centre on the ground, +Z = side the section fell towards (street). large ~13 x 13 m, small ~7 x 7 m (see bbox)
notes.slab_hanging: slab_floor frame (x 0..3.2, -z inward): floor slab of the storey above hanging diagonally from its interior support line (hinge = slab top at y = H, z = -W) down to the floor below (free edge y ~ 0.05, z ~ -1.6). With the generic minX/minY/maxZ normalisation the hinge sits at (x, H - bbox_min.y, -W - bbox_max.z)

rubble.notes: origin = ground centre of the pile, +Y up. One mesh per file, material "debris" (1024^2 atlas). rubble_1 big panel-fragment pile, rubble_2 brick-heavy pile, rubble_3 collapsed floor slabs "tent", rubble_4 low street debris, rubble_5 loose panel slab with rebar, rubble_6 brick scatter, rubble_7 big panel-slab collapse heap (~1.8 m, vehicles climb it), rubble_8 red-brick house collapse heap, rubble_9 mixed household debris pile, rubble_10 floor-slab ramp on a low mound, rubble_11 wide low concrete scatter, rubble_12 silicate-brick heap. The game rasterises each pile into a height map (src/world/terrain.js templateHeights) so vehicles drive up and over it.

trees.notes: Top-level nodes laid out 9 m apart along +X (game uses each node as a template). Origin at trunk base. Names avoid matching two city.js classes: bare=tree_*, leafy=leafy_summer_*, stump_*, fallen_trunk. Materials: bark_<species> (tiling), wood_splintered, leaves_late_summer (alpha MASK 0.5, double sided), soil.

wires.notes: Poles: origin at ground, wire run along local +X, crossarm along local Z; attach_* empties are children of the pole node, positions given in pole-local glTF coords. utility_pole_broken: snapped at 1.3 m, top hanging on rebar (attach points follow the fallen top - the game should treat it as a broken pole). trolleybus_pole: attach_0 = span-wire strain insulator (6.9 m, road side +Z), attach_1 = feeder (6.25 m). concertina_coil: 6 m stretched coil along X, 0.9 m dia; barbed_wire_fence: 3 m segment along X with one snapped strand.

props.notes: One material (props_atlas 2048^2). Origin = ground centre of footprint, forward +Z, nodes laid out on a grid in the file. garage_unit* are 3.6 m wide modules (city.js places 4 side by side at 3.6 m) with doors to +Z. crater_* are positive meshes (ejecta rim + scorched bowl texture down to y=0.02, nothing below ground). car_vaz2107_wreck_side lies on its side.

module.why: 3.2 m is the transverse-wall step of II-49 / 1-464 variants and the contract grid of src/world/buildings.js; 2.8 m storey is the contract value (real 1-464: 2.5 m clear + 0.2 m slab ~ 2.7 m, II-49: 2.64-2.8 m) - kept for gameplay clearance and because every kit piece tiles on it.

openings_m.format: x0, y0, x1, y1 in panel coords (sill 0.86 m, head 2.30 m)

panel_section_m.note: three-layer panel; the broken-edge texture and geometry rings follow these layer depths

series.1-464 (khrushchyovka, 4-5 storeys): large-panel, cross walls of room size; WHE report 55 gives storey height 2.7 m, cross-wall span 2.7 / 3.6 m, room-size wall and floor panels, welded then monolithic joints (source: World Housing Encyclopedia report 55, Series 122/135/1-464c). Facades: small glazed ceramic tile on the panels, dark mastic in the joints, a coloured tile band under the windows; no lift, low parapet, flat roof.
series.1-468 / 1-480 (Ukrainian khrushchyovka/b: same 3.2 m step family, 5 and 9 storeys, 3-layer external panels 0.30-0.35 m (concrete / mineral wool / concrete), balconies on hanging slabs with steel railings and corrugated asbestos-cement parapet sheets.
series.II-49 / II-18 (9-12 storeys): step 3.2 m, storey ~2.64-2.8 m, single- or 3-layer ceramsite-concrete panels ~0.3 m, lift machine rooms and parapets on the roof, entrance canopies (precast slab on steel tie rods) over each stair door, stairwell windows at the half-landing.
details used: double wooden casements with a "fortochka" vent, white paint peeling; replacement white PVC units
balconies glazed by residents with mismatched wood/PVC frames, boarded panes, corrugated asbestos sheets
steel entrance door with intercom, concrete canopy, basement plinth with vent grilles
paper-tape crosses on window glass (blast protection), OSB boards over blown-out windows

war_damage_reference (Mariupol, Bakhmut,: black soot plumes rising from window heads after apartment fires, licking the reveals
shell penetrations through the spandrel merging with window openings, broken edges showing the insulation layer
hanging and bent rebar mesh, chunks still tied to bars, rebar of balcony roots dangling
facade tiles blown off around impacts, dense shrapnel pockmarks with light chipped halos, diagonal cracks from opening corners
pancaked vertical slices and collapsed top corners: stubs of lower panels with bars sticking up, slabs hinged down
debris fans at the base: panel fragments, bricks, window frames, radiators, furniture, insulation
shrapnel-stripped trees: snapped limbs, splintered trunks, a few still in leaf; pollarded city poplars
concrete SV-95 utility poles with pin insulators and cobra-head lamps; trolleybus span wires cut and hanging
research.note: All geometry/textures are procedurally generated by the scripts in tools/blender/env (no third-party assets).

city.refs: Photo record of Mariupol (Livoberezhnyi / Primorskyi private sector, Azovstal-side districts), Bakhmut, Avdiivka (Khimik), Sievierodonetsk: above-ground foil-clad heating mains on concrete sleepers with П-shaped expansion loops over paths, white silicate brick transformer kiosks with louvred steel doors, ПО-2 diamond-relief concrete fences, one-storey plastered / brick houses with tin or asbestos-slate gable roofs and blue carved window trims, profiled-sheet and picket fences with painted gates, small white Orthodox churches with blue starred / gilded onion domes, MAF market pavilions with roller shutters, concrete SV lamp posts. church_small: late-19th-c. Russian-Revival parish church of the Donbas type, as rebuilt / restored in the 2000s (refs: St. Demetrius, Verkhnotoretske 1850-61 -- bell tower razed 1938, rebuilt 2020-21, shelled 26 Mar 2022: facades, roof, windows; Sviatohirsk Lavra 2022 -- windows/doors blown in, sketes burnt; Mariupol St. Michael (1997) and St. Nicholas; Kostiantynivka St. Ihor -- several domes destroyed; Dobropillia St. Ambrose -- large facade holes, roof stripped; Pokrovsk St. Vladimir -- wall damage, roof lost; reported crosses shot down by shelling). Features used: tower-refectory-nave-apse "ship" plan, bell tower over the west entrance (chetverik with a perspective portal, open arched belfry with bells, octagon + onion), refectory (trapeznaya), square nave crowned by keel kokoshniks over a dentil cornice, five domes (big drum with arched windows, four corner cupolas on drums), eight-pointed crosses with the slanted footrest, semicircular east apse, white lime render with pale-blue recessed panels and pilasters, keel-arched window surrounds, green standing-seam sheet roofs with gutters, blue onion with gold stars and gilded cupolas.
city.notes: One material (city_atlas 2048^2, tools/blender/env/city_atlas.py). Every node is a top-level mesh, origin on the ground at the footprint centre, front = +Z, nodes laid out on a grid in the file (city.js instancing ignores the layout transform). Linear pieces run along local X: pipe_straight_* 6.0 m (mains at z = +-0.36, axis y = 1.0, supports at x = +-1.5 so segments tile every 6 m), pipe_loop 6.0 m (raised to 5 m over a footpath), fence_po2_* 4.0 m panel (+0.1 m gap at the 4.1 m pitch), fence_house_* 18 m with a gate at the centre. house_* plinth 0.45 + walls to 3.2 m, gable roofs; house_c is burnt and roofless, house_b has a roof hole, house_d a shell hole in its right wall (fit inside a 19 x 18 m plot, fences at z+9 / x+-9.5). lamp_* arm reaches +Z 2 m at 9.3 m. car_parked_* length along Z (front +Z). sign_road_* plate faces +Z. church_small (church.py) is the only node with two materials: city_atlas (plinth, steps, loose bricks, glass shards) + church_atlas (1024^2, church_atlas.py; plaster / pocked / soot / brick / blue panels / standing-seam tin / gold / stripped gold / starred blue / windows / door / icon + bell bronze / rusty steel / interior / boards + char). +Z = west front with the porch and steps, -Z = east apse; main cross top at 23 m, bell-tower cross ~19.5 m. Damage: shell hole through the nave +X wall (exposed brick reveals, broken pilaster, plaster spalled, scorch, rubble and a fallen beam inside / outside), shrapnel-pocked +X facades, main dome skin torn on the +X side exposing ribs and hoops with sheets hanging, front-right cupola stripped and its cross shot off (lying on the ground at +X), bell-tower onion dented / stripped, one cupola cross bent, burnt-out refectory window on -X with a soot plume, broken windows, torn roof sheets, torn downpipe.

farmland.notes: Two materials: farmland_atlas (2048^2 opaque, tools/blender/env/farmland_atlas.py, shares city_atlas regions/seeds for brick/slate/tin/wood/concrete) and farmland_foliage (2048^2 RGBA, alphaMode MASK 0.5, double sided, farmland_foliage.py: leaf clusters, twig sprays, far-LOD crown clumps, crop parts, wattle weave, greenhouse film). Every node is a top-level mesh, origin on the ground at the footprint centre, +Y up, metres, front = +Z; nodes are laid out on a grid in the file (farmland.js instancing ignores the layout transform). Foliage vertices carry bent normals (custom split normals, outward from the crown ellipsoid) and COLOR_0 (baked crown self-shadow); buildings / wrecks carry COLOR_0 for ground AO, soot and scorch, so materials load with vertexColors. Trees/bushes: each <name>_lod1 has the same origin and silhouette (trunk prism + crown clump cards on the dense far_* cells), 50-230 tris, meant for > ~190 m. Crops (sunflower_dead_clump, corn_dry_clump, weeds_tall_clump) are foliage-only alpha cards for heavy instancing. Linear pieces lie along +X centred on the origin: fence_wattle / fence_wood_village / gate_village 3.0 m, trench_segment 6.0 m (ends open so segments chain), berm_earth ~9 m. barn_kolkhoz(_damaged) 60.9 x 12.9 m, machine_shed 31 x 16 m (long axes X). trench_segment: dark floor at y=0.03 between revetted walls, parapets up to 0.62 m (+Z) / 0.45 m (-Z), sandbag lip on the +Z parapet. Vehicles face +Z.
farmland.refs: Photo record of Kharkiv / Kherson / Zaporizhzhia oblast farmland 2022-24: black locust (Robinia) + Lombardy poplar + oak shelterbelts (lesopolosa) with elder / dog-rose understory, shell-stripped half-dead acacias; kolkhoz cowsheds of white silicate brick with asbestos-slate roofs and plank end gates (many with caved-in roofs after shelling), open steel machinery sheds, corrugated grain bins with bucket elevators, Rozhnovsky water towers, MTZ-80/82 Belarus tractors, burnt SK-5 Niva combines in fields, 2PTS-4 trailers, round bales and traditional stogs, village yards with wattle (pleten) and picket fences, sheet-steel sunburst gates, concrete-ring wells with windlass roofs, Soviet mosaic bus shelters, roadside crosses with rushnyky, trench lines and dugouts with wattle / plank revetments and sandbag lips.

fortifications.notes:
Builds assets/env/fortifications.glb: dressing for the field fortifications that src/world/terrain.js cuts INTO the
ground (trench walls / floors / spoil are the game's terrain mesh -- raw earth; these pieces only dress them).
Modelled on the 2023-25 photo / drone-footage record of Ukrainian and Russian positions: mostly unrevetted hand-dug
earth, revetment improvised and patchy -- pallets, scavenged doors, corrugated and plywood / OSB sheets, brushwood,
a few logs, wire-mesh panels on engineered stretches -- sandbags at some firing places only, pallets and planks
thrown into the mud, litter (zinc ammo tins, cans, ration pouches, cardboard, plastic), overhead cover of garnished
camouflage net, cut branches, tarpaulins and (2024-25) anti-drone fishing nets on poles, low overgrown log-and-earth
dugouts (blindazh) and crude covered MG positions, concrete "dragon's teeth".
Materials: farmland_atlas + farmland_foliage (same atlases / cache as farmland.glb, so they match the village set)
and fort_extra (tools/blender/env/fort_atlas.py: nets, tarps, plastic, boards, cardboard, labels; alpha, 2-sided).
Conventions (metres, +Y up):
  rv_pallet / rv_door / rv_sheet / rv_ply / rv_branches / rv_logs / rv_mesh
                   improvised revetment, natural size: origin at the bottom centre ON THE TRENCH FLOOR, width along X,
                   face looking +Z (into the trench), thickness behind (-Z).  The game leans it back against the
                   battered wall and may squash Y to fit the trench depth.  Widths 0.8 / 0.84 / 0.95 / 1.22 / 1.3 /
                   1.6 / 1.5 m, heights 1.2 / 2.0 / 1.8 / 1.25 / 1.3 / 1.0 / 1.5 m.
  floor_pallet / floor_planks   lying in the mud, origin on the floor, long axis X.
  litter_a / litter_b           small litter heaps (ammo tins, cans, bottle / cardboard, pouches, plastic), on floor.
  sandbag_row (1.3 m along X, two untidy courses) / sandbag_pile (heap)   origin bottom centre, front +Z.
  debris_conc      broken concrete and bricks thrown on the spoil (urban positions), origin on the ground.
  net_cover / branch_cover / tarp_cover / net_drone
                   overhead cover laid across a trench: long axis X ALONG the trench (3.2 / 2.4 / 2.0 / 4.0 m), Z across
                   (2.6 / 2.4 / 2.2 / 2.0 m, the game scales Z to the trench width + lips); origin centre at lip level.
  dugout_roof(_b)  low earth-covered log roof 4.7 x 4.9 m (x +-2.35, z +-2.45), grassed over (b: netted + branches);
                   the timbered doorway drops to y=-1.7 at z=+2.45 (the passage arrives from +Z).
  mg_nest_roof     crude log roof on 4 posts over a firing cell, embrasure to +Z; origin at ground level, cell centre.
  dragon_tooth(_b) concrete pyramid, base 1.2 m, 1.0 m tall (b: chipped, toppled-looking); origin base centre.
  dragon_tooth_rubble  a tooth blown apart: broken stump, face slabs + lumps scattered ~2 m, bent rebar; origin base
                   centre.  City.damageFortAt() swaps teeth to _b (damaged / toppled) and _rubble (destroyed).
  ammo_crates      a few wooden ammunition boxes, origin on the floor.
  tree_*_mid       mid-distance LODs of the farmland.glb trees (build_forest_lods.py), same origins / crowns.
